title: Trump Cancels Kansas and Iowa Rallies for Phone Sprint; Vance Scraps Minnesota Event
dek: The president will address voters by phone in a 72-hour push across at least 19 states, after scrapping two weekend rallies, while Vance canceled a Friday news conference without giving a reason.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The west front of the United States Capitol building in Washington, D.C.

keyPoints: Trump canceled planned weekend rallies in Kansas (Saturday) and Iowa (Sunday) and will instead hold tele-rallies, according to CNBC and Reuters.
The Republican National Committee said the president would reach at least 19 states in a "72-hour sprint" before Tuesday's elections.
Vance canceled a Friday news conference in St. Cloud, Minnesota, on the administration's "War on Fraud" effort; officials did not give a reason.
CNBC reports Trump has campaigned at 25 rallies this month and that his approval rating has fallen to historic lows.
body:
President Donald Trump has canceled two weekend rallies in the final days of the midterm campaign and will instead address voters by phone, CNBC and Reuters reported on Thursday and Friday. The planned stops in Kansas, on Saturday, and Iowa, on Sunday, were part of a midterm schedule Trump had said would take him to 35 locations.

## A phone-based sprint

The Republican National Committee said the president would reach at least 19 states in a "72-hour sprint" before Election Day on Nov. 3. RNC Chairman Joe Gruters said voters "want to hear from President Trump before Election Day." CNBC reported that Trump has campaigned at 25 rallies this month and acknowledged the strain of a dense schedule, saying in Mississippi on Monday that he could not do a rally every day.

## Vance event scrapped

Vice President JD Vance also canceled a Friday news conference in St. Cloud, Minnesota, where he was to appear with members of the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud to announce the "War on Fraud" effort, according to the White House. The reason for the cancellation was not stated.

CNBC reported that Trump's approval rating has dropped to historic lows, amid frustration over gasoline prices and the prolonged war with Iran. Earlier this week Trump campaigned for Sen. Darline Graham in Rock Hill, South Carolina, as covered in Wire's Oct. 29 story.

## Context for the closing stretch

CNBC reported that Trump said he would travel to 35 locations in the midterm blitz; the cancellations reduce the in-person portion of that schedule. The White House and RNC did not give a reason for the Vance cancellation, and CNBC reported that the reason "remains unclear."

The Reuters report on the rally cancellations described the change as a shift toward phone-based events in the final days before the vote. Trump's approval rating is described by CNBC as having fallen to historic lows, with voters frustrated over gasoline prices and the prolonged conflict with Iran. This story will be updated if the White House or RNC provides a reason for the Vance cancellation or if Trump schedules additional in-person events.
